name: NIAD Art Center
summary: NIAD Art Center is a nonprofit studio in Richmond, California for adult artists with developmental and physical disabilities, founded in 1982, where staff support artists in creating and selling work.
notes: www.niadart.org 301-redirects to niadart.org (final 200 OK, curl-verified). Site does not state a leadership model explicitly.

name: Creativity Explored
summary: Creativity Explored is a San Francisco studio founded in 1983 by Florence Ludins-Katz and Elias Katz that gives adults with developmental disabilities studio access, materials, and professional support to create and sell art.
notes: Curl 200 OK. Site language is 'partners with artists with developmental disabilities'; run by professional staff, not artist-governed.

name: Project Onward
summary: Project Onward is a nonprofit studio and gallery in Chicago, founded in 2004 out of the city's Gallery 37 youth program, providing studio space, materials, and career support to more than 60 adult artists with disabilities and mental illness.

name: Pure Vision Arts
summary: Pure Vision Arts is a studio and exhibition space in New York City, founded in 2002 as a program of The Shield Institute, staffed by art-education and art-therapy professionals who support artists with autism and other developmental disabilities.
notes: purevisionarts.org 301-redirects to www.purevisionarts.org (final 200 OK, curl-verified).

name: LAND Gallery
summary: LAND Studio & Gallery is a nonprofit day-habilitation program in Brooklyn, NY, founded in 2005 by the League Education and Treatment Center, teaching life skills through art alongside professional artists.

name: Passion Works Studio
summary: Passion Works Studio is a nonprofit collaborative art studio in Athens, Ohio, creating paid creative work for artists with and without developmental disabilities, best known for its handmade Passion Flowers.
notes: Founding year not stated on official pages checked (site references '20 years' of undated copy and Patty Mitchell working there 'since 1994'); could not independently verify this session. 'mixed' leadership reflects the site's own framing as 'creative people with and without developmental differences' working collaboratively, plus 'we wanted to create an organization that follows the lead, talent and interests of our artists.'

name: Arts Project Australia
summary: Arts Project Australia is a Melbourne studio and gallery founded in 1974 by Myra Hilgendorf, the first full-time art studio in Australia dedicated to artists with intellectual disability, now supporting more than 150 artists.
notes: Site's own tagline calls itself an organisation 'championing neurodivergent artists and artists with intellectual disability.'

name: Studio A
summary: Studio A is a supported studio based in St Leonards, Sydney, led by CEO/Artistic Director Gabrielle Mordy, providing professional development and commercial representation to artists with intellectual disability.
notes: Founding year not stated on the mission/impact pages checked; could not verify this session.

name: Atelier Incurve
summary: Atelier Incurve (renamed INCURVE in April 2024) is a licensed day-service art facility in Osaka operated by the Social Welfare Corporation Sou-kai for adults with intellectual disabilities under Japan's disability-support law.
notes: Site confirms operation by Social Welfare Corporation Sou-kai and the 2024 rename to INCURVE, but does not state the studio's original founding year on pages checked.

name: Able Art Japan
name_local: エイブル・アート・ジャパン
summary: Able Art Japan is a Tokyo NPO founded in 1995 that supports people with disabilities in creating, exhibiting, and selling art; it co-founded the affiliated Able Art Company (2007), an agency licensing disabled artists' work commercially.
notes: Related entity Able Art Company (https://ableartcom.jp/, curl 200 OK) is an artist agency founded 2007 by three Japanese NPOs including Able Art Japan, HQ in Nara with a Tokyo office. Neither site explicitly claims artist-led governance; language is 'together with people with disabilities.'

name: Debajo del Sombrero
summary: Debajo del Sombrero is a Madrid nonprofit platform, active since 2007, running an assisted art studio and gallery where professional staff accompany artists with intellectual disabilities in creating, exhibiting, and selling contemporary art.
notes: debajodelsombrero.org (alternate domain) timed out on curl (20s connection timeout) and was not used; debajodelsombrero.es returned 200 OK. 2007 founding date is from third-party arts-press coverage (masdearte.com, mediacionartistica.org) found before search quota ran out, not an explicit dated claim on the official site itself.

name: Kunsthuis Yellow Art
summary: An art studio in Geel, Belgium for people with psychiatric or mental-health vulnerabilities, established as a permanent facility in 2004 by OPZ Geel, a public psychiatric care center; professional artists collaborate with about 30 participants outside a therapeutic framework.
notes: Linked to OPZ Geel (public psychiatric hospital); grew out of the 2001 'Y.E.L.L.O.W.' exhibition curated by Jan Hoet. Serves psychiatric patients broadly, not a disability-specific studio.

name: La "S" Grand Atelier
summary: A center for art brut and contemporary art in Vielsalm, Belgium, founded in 1992 by director Anne-Francoise Rouche as a creative workshop for artists with intellectual disabilities, which also hosts professional artists for co-creation residencies.
notes: Official site is live (HTTP 200) but currently shows only an 'under reconstruction' placeholder — facts sourced from BPS22's exhibition page and the Vielsalm tourism site instead. Recognized as a Centre d'Art Brut & Contemporain by the Wallonia-Brussels Federation in 2019.

name: Atelier Herenplaats
summary: An art studio and gallery in Rotterdam, Netherlands, founded in 1991, providing studio space and training for about 35 artists with intellectual disabilities or psychiatric backgrounds, supervised by professional artists and art teachers.

name: Atelier Goldstein
summary: An artist studio in Frankfurt, Germany, founded in 2001 as a project of Lebenshilfe Frankfurt, offering individual artistic assistance from professional artists to people with cognitive disabilities; work has shown at documenta fifteen and Schirn Kunsthalle.
notes: Site's WAF returns HTTP 500 on plain HEAD requests but 200 on GET (verified live via GET and WebFetch).

name: Kunstwerkstatt der Lebenshilfe Berlin
summary: An inclusive art workshop run by Lebenshilfe Berlin in Berlin, Germany, active since at least 1999 (its first exhibition), where professional facilitators guide clients with intellectual disabilities in painting and other visual art.
notes: Domain works reliably only over plain HTTP; HTTPS fails TLS handshake. Exact founding year not stated on-site — earliest documented activity is its 1999 exhibition.

name: Back to Back Theatre
summary: Contemporary theatre company in Geelong whose ensemble consists of actors with disability; founded 1987, led by non-disabled Artistic Director Bruce Gladwin with a full-time disabled ensemble at its creative core.
notes: Ensemble members are neurodivergent/disabled; Artistic Director Bruce Gladwin is not disclosed as disabled. No 'led by disabled people' claim found on site.

name: Restless Dance Theatre
summary: Adelaide-based inclusive contemporary dance company founded in 1991 by Sally Chance and Tania Rose, building careers for disabled and neurodivergent dancers.
notes: Founded by non-disabled artists. Company's own history notes a former artistic director (2009) was 'the first artistic director with a disability in any Australian dance company', and current AD Michelle Ryan (since 2013) has MS — but no blanket 'disability-led' institutional claim, so kept as mixed.

name: Mind the Gap
summary: Bradford-based learning disability and autism performance and live-arts company founded in 1988 by Tim Wheeler and Susan Brown; learning disabled and autistic artists co-create productions and help steer the company's creative work.
notes: Site states artists 'directly influence and steer' the work and its vision is a world where 'learning disabled and autistic voices lead the way' — aspirational/future-tense, not a present-tense 'led by' claim. Current joint CEOs show no disability disclosure.

name: Theater HORA
summary: Zurich ensemble theatre founded in 1993 by Michael Elber, part of Stiftung Züriwerk since 2002; all ensemble actors have a certified cognitive/learning disability, while artistic and overall direction is held by non-disabled staff.
notes: 18 full-time ensemble actors are IV-certified with cognitive disability; overall/artistic direction is non-disabled. 'Freie Republik HORA' lab (since 2013) lets ensemble members direct/choreograph their own work.

name: Compagnie de l'Oiseau-Mouche
summary: Roubaix theatre company founded in 1978 (professionalized 1981) as France's first artistic ESAT, with a permanent troupe of actors with intellectual/psychological disability directed by rotating outside stage directors.
notes: General/artistic direction held by non-disabled staff; productions staged by guest directors. Permanent troupe of ~20-23 comédien·ne·s have intellectual/psychological disability.

name: Teatro La Plaza
summary: Theatre in Lima, Peru, founded in 2003 by a group of artists including director Chela De Ferrari (non-disabled); internationally known for productions 'Hamlet' (2021) and 'Ricardo III' (2023), which cast actors with Down syndrome.
notes: General theatre venue directed by non-disabled founder; Down-syndrome casting applies to specific acclaimed productions, not a standing disabled ensemble. Site blocks some browser user-agents (403 on one UA, 200 on another) — confirmed live either way.

name: Theater Thikwa
summary: Berlin theatre company founded in 1991, self-described as a company where artists 'with and without disability' make theatre together; artistic direction is currently shared by Nicole Hummel and Laura Besch.

name: Blue Apple Theatre
summary: Winchester, UK theatre company founded in 2005 by Jane Jessop, producing theatre, dance, singing and film with performers who have learning disabilities; operates as a working name of the Minstead Trust charity.
notes: Founded by Jane Jessop (non-disabled), mother of company member Tommy Jessop, who has Down syndrome; site separates 'Performers' from 'Staff/Facilitators/Trustees'.

name: Hijinx Theatre
summary: Cardiff-based inclusive theatre company founded in 1981 by Gaynor Lougher and Richard Berry; centers learning disabled and/or autistic artists as its core ensemble, currently under co-CEOs Ben Pettitt-Wade and Eloise Tong.
notes: Founders and current leadership are not disclosed as disabled; org's own language centers learning disabled/autistic artists as creative contributors without stating they hold governance roles.

name: Cia. Teatral Ueinzz
summary: Theatre company in São Paulo, founded around 1997, whose ensemble mixes users of mental health/psychiatric services with professional actors and philosophers, closely associated with philosopher Peter Pál Pelbart.
notes: No dedicated official website found; sources vary on exact founding year (1996-1999). Confirmed active via a May 2024 performance listing. Peter Pál Pelbart is named as an actor-coordinator/member, not simply an outside academic observer. (original url https://x.com/ueinzz was a social-media link; replaced with source page)

name: Frente de Artistas del Borda
summary: Arts collective founded in 1984 inside Buenos Aires' Borda psychiatric hospital, made up of current and former patients working alongside community members and professionals across theatre, music, and visual-arts workshops.
notes: Blog itself dormant since ~2012, but org's continued activity confirmed via 40th-anniversary (2024) press coverage and a live YouTube channel. A commonly cited domain, frentedeartistasdelbord.com, does not resolve (dead).

name: DaDaFest
summary: Biennial disability and Deaf arts festival in Liverpool produced by DaDa, a self-described disability-controlled/disability-led arts organisation with roots to 1984; the festival launched in 2001.
notes: Parent org DaDa traces roots to 1984 (as Arts Integrated Merseyside/North West Disability Arts Forum); DaDaFest festival itself began 2001.

name: Unlimited
summary: UK commissioning body backing new work by disabled artists since 2012, delivered in partnership by disability-led charity Shape Arts and producer Artsadmin, staging periodic festivals in London.
notes: Originally conceived by Arts Council England for the 2012 Cultural Olympiad; delivery partnership pairs disability-led Shape Arts with Artsadmin, which is not disability-led per available sources — hence 'mixed' rather than 'nd-led'.

name: Oska Bright Film Festival
summary: Biennial film festival in Brighton founded in 2004 by learning-disabled filmmakers, screening only films made by or featuring learning-disabled and/or autistic people, run today by a learning-disabled programming team under Carousel.

name: Superfest International Disability Film Festival
summary: Longest-running disability film festival in the world, founded in 1970, now produced by the Paul K. Longmore Institute on Disability and the San Francisco Disability Cultural Center in the Bay Area.
notes: Leadership marked unknown: sources confirm disabled people serve as judges but do not explicitly state staff/leadership disability status.

name: ReelAbilities Film Festival: New York
summary: Film festival dedicated to disability representation on and off screen, founded in 2007 at the Marlene Meyerson JCC Manhattan and now the flagship of a touring ReelAbilities network across the US.
notes: Leadership marked unknown: available sources name JCC Manhattan and co-directors but do not state whether disabled people hold leadership/staff roles.

name: The Museum of Everything
summary: UK registered charity and travelling museum for self-taught, art brut and outsider art, founded by James Brett in London in 2009; operates the Gallery of Everything, its commercial space on Chiltern Street.
notes: Site 301-redirects to musevery.com (HTTP 200). Curated by founder James Brett, not by ND/disabled people themselves. Touring model plus fixed Gallery of Everything retail space; recent (2025/26) exhibition dates not independently confirmed.

name: Collection de l'Art Brut
summary: The founding art brut museum, opened 1976 in Château de Beaulieu, Lausanne, from Jean Dubuffet's 1971 donation of ~5,000 works to the city; now holds over 60,000 pieces.
notes: Curatorial institution run by the City of Lausanne, not artist-led. Many original works came from psychiatric patients, but the collection deliberately spans self-taught/marginal creators beyond that population.

name: Museum Gugging
summary: Art brut complex in Maria Gugging (Klosterneuburg) built around the Haus der Künstler, a residence-studio for artists with psychiatric/intellectual disabilities opened 1981 under psychiatrist Leo Navratil; the museum building dates to 2006.
notes: Museum itself operated by NÖ Museum Betriebs GmbH under artistic director Johann Feilacher (psychiatrist), not by the resident artists. The adjacent galerie gugging (separate site, galeriegugging.com) is owned by the Gugging Artists collective — worth a separate look if a more nd-led entry is wanted.

name: Dr. Guislain Museum
summary: Museum of the history of psychiatry and outsider art, housed in Belgium's oldest psychiatric hospital (inaugurated 1857) in Ghent, founded on the reform work of Dr. Joseph Guislain.
notes: Exact year the museum (as opposed to the 1857 hospital) opened to the public could not be confirmed from primary sources; secondary sources vary (1980s). Run by the Guislain psychiatric institution/foundation, not by patients or an nd-led body.

name: Bethlem Museum of the Mind
summary: Museum of mental health history and patient art on the grounds of Bethlem Royal Hospital (Beckenham), opened in its current Art Deco building in March 2015 as the public face of the Bethlem Art and History Collections Trust (est. 1970).
notes: Run by the hospital-linked charitable trust; archive/collection roots go back to 1970. Distinct from the separate Bethlem Gallery, which is more directly artist-facing.

name: Prinzhorn Collection
summary: Collection of art by psychiatric patients assembled by Hans Prinzhorn at Heidelberg University's psychiatric clinic from 1919, with a dedicated museum inaugurated in 2001; now ~40,000 works from 1825 to today.
notes: Part of Heidelberg University Hospital; a research/curatorial institution, not patient- or artist-run.

name: Raw Vision
summary: Quarterly print and online magazine devoted to outsider art and art brut, founded by John Maizels in London in 1989 and now headquartered in Radlett, Hertfordshire.
notes: Edited/founded by art historian John Maizels, not by neurodivergent or disabled staff explicitly.

name: The Art of Autism
summary: San Diego-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit, founded 2005, that promotes autistic artists via an online gallery, exhibits and film festivals; states its board is approximately 50% autistic.
notes: Explicitly self-reports ~50% autistic board composition on its own fact sheet; active with content through August 2026.

name: Heart n Soul
summary: South East London arts organisation making music and performance work, originating from 1984 creative sessions in Lewisham and formally founded 1987; explicitly led by people with and without learning disabilities and autistic people.
notes: Founding date varies across sources (1984 workshops, 1986 performance company, 1987 per Shape Arts timeline); leadership language ('led by people with and without learning disabilities and autistic people') is the org's own self-description.

name: Neuk Collective
summary: Scotland-wide community and advocacy network for neurodivergent artists, run under Door in the Wall Arts Access CIC (a disabled-led organisation) and founded by neurodivergent textile artist Tzipporah Johnston.
notes: Exact founding year not stated on the site (its own 'Our story'/'history' subpages 404'd during verification); currently active with a directory, membership, and a 2026 Glasgow exhibition.
